findings.issue_text: Fallback locales are only ensured for web requests: I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is invoked solely from ApplicationController#set_locale, while the translate accelerator loads only the active locale, so mailers (which set I18n.locale per recipient) and background jobs never load the fallback locales — the backend walks [user_locale, site_default, :en], misses on the unloaded locales, and returns MissingTranslation, meaning the fallback feature silently doesn't work for emails and jobs, with each miss paying a full uncached 3-locale chain walk on every interpolated call

SiteSetting.default_locale is read on every FallbackLocaleList#[] computation on the hottest path in the app: interpolated/pluralized I18n.t calls bypass the accelerator cache, so any key with partial coverage in the user's locale recomputes the fallback chain (a settings-provider staleness check plus fresh Array with to_sym/uniq/compact allocations) on every single call, hundreds of times per rendered page; it should be memoized per locale (invalidated on site-setting change) or computed once in set_locale

Locale-loading cache is append-only with no eviction: every request ensures the user locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, and :en are parsed from YAML and retained in @translations for the life of the process, forcing the multi-MB :en tree into every process even for monolingual non-English sites, and multilingual or multisite deployments permanently accumulate one full parsed tree per locale ever seen, materially raising the per-process memory floor

The lazy locale load is unsynchronized: the check-then-act in ensure_loaded!/load_locale has no mutex, so all boot-time request threads can parse the same locales concurrently, wasting CPU, producing duplicate @loaded_locales entries, and causing a latency spike after every deploy

goldens.comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fallback locales are only ensured for web requests: I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is invoked solely from ApplicationController#set_locale, while the translate accelerator loads only the active locale, so mailers (which set I18n.locale per recipient) and background jobs never load the fallback locales — the backend walks [user_locale, site_default, :en], misses on the unloaded locales, and returns MissingTranslation, meaning the fallback feature silently doesn't work for emails and jobs, with each miss paying a full uncached 3-locale chain walk on every interpolated call

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows fallback loading is explicitly triggered only in `ApplicationController#set_locale` via `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`, and `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` is the only place that eagerly loads the whole fallback chain (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`). Other execution contexts (mailers/background jobs) are not shown calling this, so they may not get the same eager loading behavior. However, whether this is an actual defect depends on how `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` interacts with the translate accelerator (e.g., whether fallback lookups invoke translations with `config.locale` switched such that `TranslateAccelerator#translate` would load those locales on demand), which is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SiteSetting.default_locale is read on every FallbackLocaleList#[] computation on the hottest path in the app: interpolated/pluralized I18n.t calls bypass the accelerator cache, so any key with partial coverage in the user's locale recomputes the fallback chain (a settings-provider staleness check plus fresh Array with to_sym/uniq/compact allocations) on every single call, hundreds of times per rendered page; it should be memoized per locale (invalidated on site-setting change) or computed once in set_locale

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a custom `FallbackLocaleList#[]` that recomputes `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` on every access, including reading `SiteSetting.default_locale` each time (config/initializers/i18n.rb). With `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` enabled, missing-translation lookups can call `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` repeatedly; combined with `translate_accelerator` explicitly bypassing its cache when `args.length > 0` (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb), it’s plausible this increases per-translation overhead. However, the specific “hottest path / hundreds of times per page” claim isn’t directly provable from the diff alone, and this is a performance/architecture concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Locale-loading cache is append-only with no eviction: every request ensures the user locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, and :en are parsed from YAML and retained in @translations for the life of the process, forcing the multi-MB :en tree into every process even for monolingual non-English sites, and multilingual or multisite deployments permanently accumulate one full parsed tree per locale ever seen, materially raising the per-process memory floor

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds per-request `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `ApplicationController#set_locale`, and the new `FallbackLocaleList#[]` always includes `:en` (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`). It also introduces `TranslateAccelerator#ensure_loaded!` which caches `@loaded_locales` with no eviction (`@loaded_locales ||= []` and only appends via `include?` checks). From the diff, locales that are ever encountered will remain "loaded" for the life of the process, and `:en` will be ensured/loaded at least once even for non-English sites. This is a memory/per-process-footprint concern rather than a functional correctness defect, and is directly grounded in the added code paths; however, the exact size/behavior of `@translations` and YAML parsing is not fully shown in this diff.
